story_type: largest conventional bomb test: parachute extraction from a cargo plane, fall and blast
hook: A 21,500 pound bomb, pulled out the back of a cargo plane.
narration: This bomb weighed twenty one thousand five hundred pounds.
Officially, it was the Massive Ordnance Air Blast. Everyone called it the Mother of All Bombs.
On March eleventh, two thousand three, the Air Force tested it over Eglin, in Florida.
It rode in a C-130 cargo plane. A parachute pulled it out the open ramp, the way heavy supplies are air dropped.
Then it fell free, steering itself toward the target.
outcome: The blast threw up a mushroom cloud that could be seen from up to twenty miles away.
title: The Mother of All Bombs test drop
description:
The Air Force tests the 21,500-pound GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb, dropped from a C-130 over Eglin, Florida, on March 11, 2003.

extra_sources.excerpt: A Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB) weapon is prepared for testing at the Eglin Air Force Armament Center on March 11, 2003. The MOAB is a precision-guided munition weighing 21,500 pounds and will be dropped from a C-130 Hercules aircraft for the test. It will be the largest non-nuclear conventional weapon in existence.

The GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb prototype moments before it makes contact during testing March 11, 2003. The detonation created a mushroom cloud that could be seen from up to 20 miles away.
